title: Finite-site comparison of the proper/open compatible-tower word
statement:
Let $R$ be a finite commutative ring. All schemes are Noetherian (they have finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings) [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Work in ordinary constant-$R$ module derived categories on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $N_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $P_v^t=Rv_*^t$ and $J_j^t=j_!^t$ ($t=e,p$). Let $d_v:N P_v^e\to P_v^pN$ be the specified counit mate [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], and $e_j:N J_j^e\to J_j^pN$ the canonical open comparison [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. Let $\kappa^t_{b,a}:P_b^tP_a^t\cong P_{ba}^t$ be the canonical derived direct-image compositor, normalized as the inverse adjunction conjugate of composite inverse image, and $m^t_{b,a}:J_b^tJ_a^t\cong J_{ba}^t$ the canonical open compositor [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. All equations below include canonical functor associators. 
Supply schemes and morphisms
$$X\xrightarrow a U\xrightarrow b\overline X\xrightarrow p\overline Y\xrightarrow q Z,\qquad Y\xrightarrow i\overline Y,\qquad s:U\to Y,$$
where $a,b,i$ are quasi-compact open immersions, $p,q,s$ are proper, $pb=is$ is Cartesian, $f=sa$ and $g=qi$. Thus $(a,s),(i,q),(ba,qp)$ compactify $f,g,gf$, respectively [def-asd-compactifiable, def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Set $F_f^t=P_s^tJ_a^t$, $F_g^t=P_q^tJ_i^t$, $F_{gf}^t=P_{qp}^tJ_{ba}^t$, and set $B_f=P_s^p(e_a)d_s(J_a^e(-))$, $B_g=P_q^p(e_i)d_q(J_i^e(-))$, $B_{gf}=P_{qp}^p(e_{ba})d_{qp}(J_{ba}^e(-))$.
Let $\Gamma^e:J_i^eP_s^e\to P_p^eJ_b^e$ be the specified etale proper/open interchange, and $\Gamma^p$ the open adjunct of inverse site-transported open-restriction exchange [lem-sp-proper-open-coefficient-mate]. For $t=e,p$ define the actual tower arrow
$$A^t:P_q^tJ_i^tP_s^tJ_a^t\xrightarrow{P_q^t(\Gamma^tJ_a^t)}P_q^tP_p^tJ_b^tJ_a^t\xrightarrow{\kappa^t_{q,p},m^t_{b,a}}P_{qp}^tJ_{ba}^t.$$
On bounded-below etale inputs $A^e$ is the restriction of the normalized unbounded compact-support compositor [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]. For $E\in D^+(X_e,R)$, define the two word comparisons
$$W_{\rm in}=P_q^pJ_i^pP_s^p(e_a)\circ P_q^pJ_i^p(d_sJ_a^e)\circ P_q^p(e_iP_s^eJ_a^e)\circ d_q(J_i^eP_s^eJ_a^e),$$
$$W_{\rm out}=P_q^pP_p^pJ_b^p(e_a)\circ P_q^pP_p^p(e_bJ_a^e)\circ P_q^p(d_pJ_b^eJ_a^e)\circ d_q(P_p^eJ_b^eJ_a^e).$$
These natural maps satisfy the word equation
$$W_{\rm out}\circ N_Z(P_q^e(\Gamma^eJ_a^e))=(P_q^p(\Gamma^pJ_a^p)N_X)\circ W_{\rm in}.$$
After the proper and open compositors, this is the equality of named maps
$$B_{gf}\circ N_Z(A^e)=(A^pN_X)\circ F_g^p(B_f)\circ B_g(F_f^e(-)).$$
In particular $A^pN_X$ is invertible and equals $B_{gf}N_Z(A^e)(F_g^p(B_f)\circ B_gF_f^e)^{-1}$. The pro-etale arrow is the open-adjunct paste above, not defined by this last transport formula. All expressions are natural in $E$; the inputs to $d$ and $\Gamma$ have bounded-below etale witnesses, including $J_a^pN_XE$ and $F_f^pN_XE$. No special presentation of $R$ or base field is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-finite-site-word-refinement] with the given finite ring and Noetherian schemes. Put $M=J_a^eE$ and $H=J_a^pN_XE$. Both have lower bounds, and $e_a(E):N_UM\xrightarrow{\sim}H$ is an etale-origin witness for $H$. The etale objects $P_s^eM$, $J_i^eP_s^eM$, $J_b^eM$, and $P_p^eJ_b^eM$ are bounded below; for the last, identify $J_b^eJ_a^e$ with $J_{ba}^e$ by the stated open compositor. The witness for $P_s^pH$ is $(P_s^eM,B_f(E))$. Thus all components of $d_s,d_p,d_q,d_{qp}$ below have bounded-below etale inputs, and every pro-etale input to $\Gamma$ has the displayed witness. The three $B$ maps are natural isomorphisms by that lemma. No coefficient extension or preservation of a lower bound under coefficient extension is being used. In Lean the three B components are composites of the specified proper comparison isomorphism and the canonical open comparison; their invertibility follows directly from these factors.

proof.text:
Use the site clause of [lem-sp-proper-open-coefficient-mate] for $(k,r,p,i)=(b,s,p,i)$ and input $M$. The required square is Cartesian by hypothesis, its vertical maps $s,p$ are proper, and its horizontal maps $b,i$ are open. Set
$$c_{\rm in}=J_i^p(d_s(M))\circ e_i(P_s^eM),\qquad c_{\rm out}=P_p^p(e_b(M))\circ d_p(J_b^eM).$$
The cited equation is exactly
$$c_{\rm out}\circ N_{\overline Y}(\Gamma^e(M))=\Gamma^p(N_UM)\circ c_{\rm in}.$$
Here $\Gamma^p$ is the specified open adjunct, not an arrow chosen to force this equality.

proof.text: Whisker the site equation of Step 2 by P_q and precompose with d_q. Apply naturality of d_q at Gamma^e(M). The definition of GP at J_a^p N_X E is the site interchange at M transported by e_a(E) and its inverse. Expand this definition and W_in/W_out, then cancel the adjacent e_a(E) followed by its inverse under the three functors. This gives the word equation for the actual specified open-adjunct paste; no additional naturality theorem for the pro-etale interchange is required.

source.place: Tag 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), four displayed equalities, using Tag 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open); agent site-comparison pasting calculation.

proof.text:
By the definitions of the three compact-support words and of $B_f,B_g$, functoriality gives
$$F_g^p(B_f(E))\circ B_g(F_f^eE)
=P_q^pJ_i^pP_s^p(e_a(E))\circ P_q^pJ_i^p(d_s(M))\circ P_q^p(e_i(P_s^eM))\circ d_q(J_i^eP_s^eM)=W_{\rm in}.$$
Only reassociation and preservation of composition by $P_q^p,J_i^p$ are involved.

proof.text:
Write $C^t=P_{qp}^t(m^t_{b,a})\circ\kappa^t_{q,p}(J_b^tJ_a^t)$, so $A^t=C^t\circ P_q^t(\Gamma^tJ_a^t)$. For the two compositors apply [lem-sp-finite-site-word-refinement], whose $d,e,\kappa,m$ have exactly the normalizations in the present statement. Put $V=J_b^eJ_a^eE$ and $h=J_b^p(e_a(E))\circ e_b(J_a^eE)$. Naturality of $\kappa^p$ moves $P_q^pP_p^p(h)$ to $P_{qp}^p(h)$ after $\kappa^p$. Its proper-composition equation, evaluated at $V$, then yields
$$C^pW_{\rm out}=P_{qp}^p(m^p_{b,a}\circ h)\circ d_{qp}(V)\circ N_Z(\kappa^e_{q,p}(V)).$$
The open-composition equation says $m^p_{b,a}\circ h=e_{ba}(E)\circ N_{\overline X}(m^e_{b,a}(E))$. Substitute this and use naturality of $d_{qp}$ at $m^e_{b,a}(E)$ to obtain
$$C^pW_{\rm out}=P_{qp}^p(e_{ba}(E))\circ d_{qp}(J_{ba}^eE)\circ N_Z(P_{qp}^e(m^e_{b,a}(E))\circ\kappa^e_{q,p}(V))=B_{gf}(E)\circ N_Z(C^e).$$
Thus both compositor squares have been applied to the actual word, with their directions fixed.

proof.text:
Postcompose the word equation of Step 3 with $C^p$. Substitute Step 5 on the left and Step 4 on the right. Since $A^t=C^tP_q^t(\Gamma^tJ_a^t)$, the resulting equation is
$$B_{gf}\circ N_Z(A^e)=(A^pN_X)\circ F_g^p(B_f)\circ B_g(F_f^e(-)).$$
This establishes the asserted equality for the open-adjunct paste defining $A^p$.

proof.text: For normalization, paste the D+ inclusion compatibility squares for the proper compositor, open compositor and specified etale interchange. Construct the compatible compactification triangle with q=b and p=p and Cartesian square sq.flip. The normalized adjunct identity of the etale interchange identifies it with the exchange used by the unbounded compact-support formalism. The formalism triangle equation then identifies AEUnbounded, through rightDerivedLowerShriekIso for the three supplied compactifications, with unboundedEtaleLowerShriekCompIso. Independently, AE is invertible because its specified interchange and both compositors are isomorphisms. The three B components are invertible, hence so is D. Cancel D in the named-map equation to obtain the inverse formula and invertibility of AP. Prove naturality of B, Win, Wout and AE from naturality of their constituent transformations (using the natural etale interchange isomorphism). Finally derive naturality of AP by cancellation of D in the natural named-map equation.
